To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a large variability of pediatric anesthesia practice across Europe is associated with a high incidence of critical events; (2) the number of pediatric cases performed by the anesthesiology staff should be taken into account for the selection of the anesthesiology provider; (3) the introduction of incident-reporting systems at the local and national levels could contribute to the harmonization of training and certification requirements for anesthesia management of pediatric cases.

the number of pediatric cases performed by the anesthesiology staff and the level of experience of the anesthesiology team are the most important variables that affect the incidence of critical events in children.

the APRICOT (Anesthesia Practice In Children Observational Trail) study showed a large variability of practice in anesthesia care for children across Europe and a large incidence of severe critical events.
